scope: Every mutable fact used by an in-scope Phase 1 allow decision plus explicitly identified later-phase carry-forward facts; this is a contract inventory, not a claim that PostgreSQL serialization has been implemented.

serialization.actor_tenant_aggregate: Retained as the actor_tenant scope row keyed by lowercase canonical tenant UUID, slash, lowercase canonical actor UUID. It is represented in the scope-version table; no duplicate actor/tenant aggregate version table exists.
serialization.command_aggregate_lock: Existing command target aggregate lock remains separate and is acquired first when the command has an aggregate target.
serialization.phase1_person_identity_scope: Excluded. Person/shared-identity and ineligibility are original Phase 2 only.
serialization.protected_command_lock_mode: SELECT ... FOR SHARE on every pre-created/ensured authority scope row; hold through authorization and business transaction commit; read source facts only after all locks are held; do not increment authority versions for a read-only authority decision.
serialization.authority_mutation_lock_mode: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the same complete scope-row set before source DML; hold through source mutation and version increments in the same transaction.
serialization.lock_order_rule: Acquire command aggregate lock first when present; acquire authority rows by scope rank (global_policy, organization, tenant, actor_tenant, actor), then COALESCE(tenant_id::text, empty string) COLLATE C, then scope_id::text COLLATE C. The unique database identity is (scope_type, tenant_id, scope_id) with NULLS NOT DISTINCT. Acquire all before source reads/writes; never request a lower-ranked key after a higher-ranked key.
serialization.database_identity: UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT (scope_type, tenant_id, scope_id)

canonical_scope_keys.tenant: (tenant, tenant_id UUID, same tenant scope_id UUID)

serialization.version_update_policy: Only a transaction that changes a mutable authority fact increments each affected scope row exactly once; protected commands do not increment versions. The source mutation and version increments commit or roll back atomically. Version and updated_at are generated by the database, never accepted from command/API input.
serialization.phase1_frozen_enforcement: symphony_app receives no INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE on frozen source tables. Only the migration/bootstrap owner may change those rows, outside serving runtime; startup/deployment validation rejects an enabled runtime mutation route or command registration for those sources.
serialization.phase1_scope_row_privileges: symphony_app has SELECT, column-level INSERT(scope_type,tenant_id,scope_id), and UPDATE(version); RLS ENABLE+FORCE scopes rows to app.tenant_id/app.actor_user_id; trigger allows only OLD.version+1 and sets updated_at. No DELETE/TRUNCATE.
serialization.rls_and_privilege_contract: RLS ENABLE and FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY. symphony_app has SELECT, INSERT(scope_type,tenant_id,scope_id), UPDATE (version); no DELETE or TRUNCATE; policies restrict tenant/actor rows.
serialization.row_provisioning: symphony_app may INSERT only tenant, organization, and actor_tenant rows for the transaction tenant, individually in canonical order before the lock pass. The ordered migration/bootstrap owner seeds the singleton global_policy row and all actor rows required by the frozen action catalogue. Runtime verifies those immutable rows exist and fails closed if any is missing; it never inserts them or retries under a privileged role.
serialization.retry: Bounded retries for SQLSTATE 40001/40P01 only, reusing the same logical command ID and transaction inputs.
serialization.proof_owner: REM-WP2.6 infrastructure/frozen-writer proof and REM-WP2.4 PostgreSQL barrier tests; REM-WP0 defines dependency coverage and expected serial outcomes.

required_invariants: Every Phase 1 allow rule references one or more applicable Phase 1 dependency IDs; Phase 2 identity-conflict facts are not Phase 1 dependencies.
The actor/tenant authority aggregate is retained exactly once as the actor_tenant row in symphony.authority_scope_versions; do not maintain a parallel aggregate version table.
Command aggregate lock, when present, is acquired before all authority scope locks; authority scope locks follow the exact inventory order and canonical key collation.
Protected commands use FOR SHARE; authority-changing commands use FOR UPDATE on the same scope rows. Both modes are held to transaction end.
Authority facts are read only after all required scope locks are held; mutable source DML and corresponding version increments occur in the same transaction.
Only authority mutation increments scope versions, exactly once per affected scope; the database generates version and updated_at values.
Every supported capacity/delegation mutation lists every affected scope, including all delegate/delegator actor_tenant rows, before it acquires locks.
Frozen Phase 1 authority sources have no serving-runtime mutation path; PostgreSQL revokes INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE from symphony_app and startup/registry checks reject runtime mutation commands.
Person/shared-identity and ineligibility facts are original Phase 2 carry-forward only and are absent from all Phase 1 scope locks and acceptance prerequisites.
A command linearized before a revocation may commit before it; a command that locks after the committed revocation must deny.
No protected mutation commits using an unlocked stale authority snapshot.
History rows are append-only; revocation changes future authority and never rewrites historical findings.
